title: Transverse Light Waves and the Electromagnetic Theory of Light
printed_title: 91. 光波的横振性和光的电磁理论

prose.text:
Light travels forward, but its oscillation can be sideways, perpendicular to the direction of travel.
This is what transverse means.

Sideways oscillation does not mean that the light itself travels only from side to side.
Maxwell's theory directly predicted that freely propagating electromagnetic waves are transverse.

Experiments had already shown that light waves are transverse before Maxwell concluded that electromagnetic waves exist.
The electromagnetic waves predicted by the theory and the light studied in experiments shared this feature.

Maxwell therefore regarded the transverse nature of light as one of the most important pieces of evidence for the electromagnetic theory of light.
Theory and experiment supported each other;
sharing this feature does not make every transverse wave a light wave.
prose.source_text: 电磁波的横振性是由麦克斯韦理论直接导出来的. 在麦克斯韦做出了电磁波存在的结论之前, 光波的横振性已经由实验证明了. 所以麦克斯韦正确地认为电磁波的横振性是对光的电磁理论的正确性的最重要的证据之一.

prose.text:
Water waves need water, and waves on a rope need a rope.
These waves spread through the mechanical motion of matter.

People once imagined that light was also a mechanical wave and invented a medium filling all space, called the ether.
To carry transverse vibrations, this imagined medium would have needed properties like those of a solid, which caused difficulties for the old explanation.

The electromagnetic theory of light does not need this mechanical ether, so it removes the difficulties caused by that assumption.
Light carries changes in electric and magnetic fields, not the shaking of a special material.

It can therefore travel through a vacuum.
The source says that electromagnetic processes follow laws of their own.

This means that field laws describe how the fields change and propagate;
laws for mechanical vibrations of a medium are not enough.

It does not mean that matter acted on by electromagnetic forces violates mechanics.
Charged objects still obey the appropriate laws of motion.
Describing changing fields and describing moving objects are connected tasks, but they are not the same task.
prose.source_text: 承认了光的电磁理论就消除了由于必须被当作固体的假想的媒质——以太而带来的所有困难. 光波不是在特殊的处处存在的媒质——以太中的机械波, 而是电磁波. 电磁过程并不遵循力学定律, 而遵循自己本身固有的定律.

prose.text:
First imagine a forward arrow showing the direction in which the light travels, and distinguish it from the directions in which the fields oscillate.
The electric field vector $\vec{E}$ and the magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$ show the sizes and directions of the local fields, like arrows with lengths.

For a plane electromagnetic wave traveling through a vacuum, these field arrows are perpendicular to each other and both are perpendicular to the direction of travel.
The source refers back to Chapter Five for this relationship.

In ordinary natural light, the oscillations of the electric field $\vec{E}$ and the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ have no stable common orientation, but different instantaneous orientations alone are not sufficient to establish that light is unpolarized.
For natural light, time or ensemble averages give equal intensities along perpendicular transverse directions, and the corresponding electric-field components have no stable phase relationship.

The independent short wave trains are uncorrelated, so the combined light has no definite polarization state.
A changing instantaneous direction alone is not enough: in circularly polarized light the transverse electric-field components have a definite phase relationship even though the electric field turns.

Circularly polarized light is therefore still polarized, not unpolarized natural light.
This does not mean that the fields oscillate in every direction at the same instant, or that the electric and magnetic fields choose their directions independently.

Within each short wave train, they are still perpendicular to each other.
Here the source's description of polarized light means plane-polarized light, also called linearly polarized light.

Other kinds of polarization also exist.
In plane-polarized light, $\vec{E}$ oscillates back and forth along a fixed sideways line, and $\vec{B}$ oscillates along another fixed sideways line perpendicular to it.

Each oscillation line and the direction of travel define a fixed plane;
these two planes are perpendicular to each other.

The oscillation line stays fixed, but the field arrow does not always point toward the same side, and its size still changes.
The source uses the polarized wave in Figure 104 as an example;
that number refers to the original book, not to a new illustration on this page.
prose.source_text: 在电磁波中矢量$\vec{E}$和$\vec{B}$彼此垂直(见第五章). 在自然光中, 电场强度$\vec{E}$和磁感应强度$\vec{B}$的振动发生在与波的传播方向垂直的所有的方向上. 如果光是偏振光, 那么无论是$\vec{E}$还是$\vec{B}$的振动都不会在所有的方向上通过, 而只能通过两个确定的平面. 图104中描述的电磁波是偏振波.

prose.text:
When we speak of the oscillation direction of light, we usually mean that of the electric field vector $\vec{E}$, rather than the magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$.
The source cites experiments showing that light's action in the eye's retina and in photographic emulsion comes mainly from the electric field acting on charged particles.

Think of a charged particle as a tiny object that an electric field can push.
A magnetic field's action on a moving charged particle also depends on the particle's speed and direction.

The source gives $\frac{c}{v}$ as the factor by which the electric force exceeds the magnetic force.
This is an approximate comparison of sizes, not a law that holds for every kind of motion.

Here $v$ is the charged particle's speed, and $c$ is the speed of light.
The comparison concerns a plane electromagnetic wave in a vacuum and uses the nonrelativistic approximation, meaning that the particle moves much more slowly than light.

For motion perpendicular to the magnetic field, the force sizes can be compared in this way.
For other directions, the magnetic force depends on the part of the velocity perpendicular to the magnetic field.

We compare corresponding characteristic sizes of the wave's fields and forces, not a ratio at an instant when both fields are zero.
If the particle moves along the magnetic field, the magnetic force is zero, so the source's factor cannot be used as a finite force ratio.

A stationary particle also has no magnetic force of this kind.
The factor is therefore neither independent of speed nor a ratio for all fields and all directions of motion.

The source estimates that electrons in atoms move at about $1\%$ of the speed of light.
This is the source's approximate scale for the comparison, not a speed shared by every electron in every atom.

At this low-speed, approximate scale, the electric force from the light is usually much larger than the magnetic force.
This helps explain why the electric field direction is normally chosen when describing light's polarization.
prose.source_text: 自然这就引起一个问题: 当讲到光波中的振动方向时, 实际上说的是哪一个矢量——$\vec{E}$还是$\vec{B}$的振动? 专门进行的实验证明了, 在眼睛的视网膜或者摄影乳剂上起作用的正是光波的电场. 这是很清楚的: 由波的电场作用在带电粒子上的力是由波的磁场作用的力的$\frac{c}{v}$倍(其中$v$是带电粒子运动的速度, $c$是光速). 因为在原子中电子的运动速度大约是光速的$1\%$, 所以电场力比磁场力要大得多.

承认了光的电磁理论就消除了由于必须被当作固体的假想的媒质——以太而带来的所有困难. 光波不是在特殊的处处存在的媒质——以太中的机械波, 而是电磁波. 电磁过程并不遵循力学定律, 而遵循自己本身固有的定律.
